one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban endorses a plan by Senate President Tito Sotto, Senator Ping Lacson, and Senator Frank Drilon -- all ending their second terms June 30 and ineligible for reelection -- to elect a new 'independent' Senate President from among the twelve holdover senators whose 2019-2025 terms keep them in office past the May 9 elections (Villar, Poe, Go, Cayetano, dela Rosa, Angara, Lapid, Marcos, Tolentino, Pimentel, Revilla, Binay). The reason is constitutional contingency: should the May 9 polls fail because of ballot-printing problems, COVID-19 disruptions, alleged data hacks, or 'any other Machiavellian excuse,' President Duterte cannot hold over (the six-year term ends hard at noon on June 30), and Article VII directs that the Senate President -- or failing him the House Speaker -- 'act as President' until one is chosen and qualified. Even a 12-member Senate, while short of a legislative quorum, can still discharge functions that do not require quorum, including providing an acting President. 'Honorable Senators, I see no harm in your plan. Just do it!' He then pivots to reader reactions to the prior Sunday's 'Embarrassing knockout' column on the Espinosa drug-case dismissal: a chorus of RTC judges, law professors, retired justices, ambassadors, civic leaders, and two incumbent justices converging on the diagnosis that sloppy police work explains the knockout, and DOJ Secretary Menardo Guevarra's pledge to vigorously prosecute Espinosa in the remaining cases (RTC-Manila, RTC-Baybay in Leyte, and one in preliminary investigation): 'He may get away in one, Chief, but he will not get away in all.' Panganiban promises that he and his readers will help monitor.
